bib.title: DeepSpeed Inference: Enabling Efficient Inference of Transformer Models at Unprecedented Scale

question: How can transformer inference, dense and MoE, be made fast and affordable across latency-critical, throughput-oriented and GPU-poor settings?
hypothesis: Memory-bandwidth-centric kernels plus inference-specific parallelism and heterogeneous-memory offload beat training-oriented inference stacks.
contributions: Single GPU transformer kernels (Deep-Fusion, SBI-GeMM) for low latency and high throughput
Many-GPU dense inference with tensor parallelism plus inference-optimized pipeline parallelism and memory optimizations
Massive-GPU sparse (MoE) inference: expert, data, tensor parallelism, PCC all-to-all, sparse kernel optimizations
ZeRO-Inference using CPU, NVMe and GPU memory

method.summary: DeepSpeed Transformer is a GPU-only stack of fused small-batch kernels, TP+PP for dense models and TP/EP/DP with optimized all-to-all for MoE. ZeRO-Inference streams weights layer by layer from DRAM or NVMe to the GPU to run huge models on few GPUs. Compared with FasterTransformer (dense) and a PyTorch MoE implementation (sparse) on A100, A6000 and V100 testbeds.
method.task: transformer (GPT-style decoder) inference serving: latency, throughput, feasibility

inference.max_tokens: dense latency: generate 8 tokens from 128-token prompt; MoE: 100 tokens from 128-token prompt, batch 8; throughput: 512-token prompt, 50 tokens generated
inference.prompting: Synthetic lengths only; no prompt text.

parameters.SBI-GeMM M: 2 for half precision, 4 for INT8 (128-byte cache line)
parameters.micro-batches: number = pipeline depth P; fewer micro-batches during token generation than during prompt processing (hybrid scheduling)
parameters.hybrid scheduling batch size: 24 (latency rises dramatically above 24, suspected PyTorch AllReduce issue)
parameters.CUDA-Graph: kernel trace stored on first launch and reused
parameters.KV offload: to CPU memory when activation memory exceeds a threshold; odd/even GPUs offload odd/even layers
parameters.ZeRO-Inference: weights pinned in DRAM or NVMe, one or few layers streamed to GPU, configurable prefetch depth

other.hardware_not_precise: Fig 6 absolute latencies only readable from plots
other.resource-constrained: max batch size possible for generating a single token

metrics.name: latency
metrics.definition: end-to-end output generation time for a batch of input prompts

baselines: PyTorch distributed MoE with TP and EP (sparse)
eval.protocol: Single configuration per point, no repeats, seeds or significance stated. Baseline and DeepSpeed use identical TP/parallelism config. Testbeds: up to 256 A100 40GB (32 DGX A100 boxes); Lambda A6000 workstation (2x A6000-48GB, 256GB DRAM, 2TB NVMe); DGX-2 V100 (16x V100-32GB, 1500GB DRAM, 30TB NVMe).

evidence.quote: a cluster of up to 256 NVIDIA Ampere A100 40GB GPUs (32 8×A100 DGX boxes [38])

results.claim: Latency reduction for sparse MoE models versus a PyTorch MoE baseline, up to 7.3x on 256 GPUs.
results.setup: 100B to 2T MoE models, up to 256 A100 40GB, same data/tensor/expert parallel config in baseline and DeepSpeed; baseline is a PyTorch MoE implementation, not FasterTransformer; per-token latency, prompt 128, batch 8
results.quote: with up to 7.3× reduction in latency
results.note: Intro contribution list says 7.2x for sparse models; abstract and Sec VII say 7.3x.

results.claim: A trillion-parameter MoE served under 25 ms.
results.setup: 1T MoE (24B+MoE-128, 1064.9B) on 256 A100 40GB, aggregate memory bandwidth 128 TB/sec
results.quote: a staggering trillion parameter MoE model can be served under 25ms

results.claim: Memory bandwidth utilization when serving the 1T MoE.
Dense model small-batch latency speedup of DeepSpeed FP16 over FasterTransformer FP16.
results.setup: Dense models 1.5B-175B, small batch, identical TP strategy; largest gain for the smallest models; prompt 128, 8 tokens generated
results.quote: DeepSpeed-FP16 achieves a speedup of up to 1.55× over the baseline

results.claim: INT8 small-batch speedup over FT FP16 baseline.
results.setup: As above; FT supports INT8 only for encoder models so baseline stays FP16
results.quote: further performance boost of up to 1.95× over the FP16 baseline

results.claim: Larger-batch latency reduction, FP16 and INT8.
results.setup: Dense models, larger batch sizes (up to 16), vs FT FP16
results.quote: DeepSpeed-FP16 reduces the latency by up to 1.57× over the baseline
results.note: INT8 gives up to 1.93x at larger batch.

results.claim: Overall dense latency gain headline (up to 1.9x vs state of the art).
results.setup: Dense models up to 175B (INT8 included), vs FasterTransformer
results.quote: latency reduction over state-of-the-art of up to 1.9× for dense models (up to 175B parameters)
results.note: Sec VII intro says 1.9x for 'hundreds of billions'; the abstract says up to 7.3x over state-of-the-art for latency overall.

results.claim: Throughput gain over best FT config for GPT-3 175B on two nodes.
results.setup: 175B on 2x8 A100, best batch size per config, prompt 512, 50 tokens generated; from better PP schedule and larger batch
results.quote: DeepSpeed Inference achieves 1.51× throughput improvement over the best FasterTransformer (FT) configuration

results.claim: 530B throughput gain over TP-only FT; FT with TP+PP crashed.
results.setup: 530B on 5 nodes (40 A100), vs TP-only FasterTransformer
results.quote: DeepSpeed Inference achieves over 1.53× throughput improvement running on 5 nodes

results.claim: ZeRO-Inference runs a 530B model on a single A6000 GPU, 25x larger than GPU-only (530B vs 20B).
results.setup: Single A6000 48GB, 256GB DRAM, 2TB NVMe; weights on NVMe/DRAM
results.quote: ZeRO-Inference can inference a 530B parameter model on a single A6000 GPU, 25× larger than the largest model that can be inferenced with a GPU-only solution

results.claim: ZeRO-Inference reaches 84 TFLOPS, 54% of the 158.4 TFLOPS peak.
results.setup: A6000, offline inference with very large batch sizes (max batch for one token)
results.quote: up to 84 TFLOPS, 54% of theoretical peak (158.4 TFLOPS)

results.claim: ZeRO-Inference beats CPU-only throughput by over 25x for models fitting CPU memory.
results.setup: Models that fit in CPU memory, A6000 workstation
results.quote: it offers over 25× higher throughput than the CPU-only solution

results.claim: Hybrid scheduling speeds prompt processing 1.18x (PP+MP) and 3.06x (MP only) over FT.
results.setup: GPT-3 175B, 2 nodes x 8 A100, batch size 24
results.quote: achieves 1.18x and 3.06x prompt processing speed-up over FasterTransformer

results.claim: MoE kernel optimizations cut MoE kernel-related latency over 6x.
results.setup: Dense-representation gating and data-layout transforms replacing sparse einsum, fused
results.quote: Combined, these optimizations result in over 6× reduction in MoE kernel-related latency.

results.claim: Faster than E.T. on small encoder models: 1.7x DistilBERT, 1.4x BERT.
results.quote: DeepSpeed Inference is 1.7x and 1.4x faster than E.T.

results.claim: PCC reduces all-to-all latency overhead from O(p) to O(p/L).
results.setup: Tensor-slicing degree L, p devices; 128 GPUs with 8-way TS: 128C1+C2 to 16C1+C2

results.claim: MT-NLG 530B needs about 1TB GPU memory just for weights.

limits: No repeats, seeds or variance reported; speedups are 'up to' maxima.
MoE speedup baseline is an unoptimized PyTorch implementation, not FasterTransformer.
FT could not run TP+PP for 530B (crashed); comparison is against TP-only.
Hybrid scheduling evaluated only at batch 24 due to a suspected PyTorch AllReduce issue, left as future work.
No accuracy evaluation; INT8 effect on quality not reported. FT INT8 not available for decoders at time of writing.
ZeRO-Inference is throughput-only and not latency-sensitive.
2022 hardware (A100/A6000/V100); superseded by continuous batching and paged KV systems, not covered here.
Absolute latencies are only in figures.

terms.definition: tiles the computation space along dimensions with no cross-tile dependencies so operators including reductions, transposes and GeMMs can fuse when each tile of the second depends on one tile of the first
Parallelism Coordinated Communication: all-to-all only within devices sharing the same tensor-slicing rank, followed by allgather
pins model weights in DRAM or NVMe and streams each layer into GPU memory, allowing large batches
